newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gasoline prices stable at the pump in January.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gasoline prices stable at the pump in January.

text.p: Gasoline prices at the pump, soaring in recent months due to sagging inventories, have held stable so far this month, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).
But AAA officials warn not to read too much into the respite in rising prices, noting stocks remain rather low.
We can't say the worst is over. We still have very low inventories," said Mike Morrisey, a AAA official in Florida.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said last week stocks are now below 200 million barrels -- a threshold industry sources consider stocks to be low.
The average price of regular self serve unleaded gasoline remains at $1.288 a gallon or nearly $0.15 over the same period last year.

Gasoline futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange have been dipping since New Years Day, but rose sharply on Tuesday amid growing views supplies are starting to dip too far below 200 million barrels for comfort.

That futures move was helped by a number of refinery maintenance projects now going on in the dense U.S. Gulf Coast refining region that are aimed at maximizing gasoline production in preparation for greater gasoline demand.

The AAA's Morissey, echoing oil industry sources, said gasoline stocks have sagged in the last few months as U.S. refiners have struggled to replenish low heating oil stocks in preparation for winter in the Northeastern heating oil market.

"As refiners have gone to their just-in-time inventory strategy, they rush to put out one fire while ignoring another," Morissey said, referring to a low stocks strategy the oil industry has been pursuing in the last 18 months to free working capital.
